## Purpose

`--load-format fastsafetensors` stages a whole shard per rank in device memory
before distributing it, so peak load memory tracks the checkpoint's shard layout
rather than the memory actually available. Where a shard is large relative to
free memory, the load runs out of memory on a model that otherwise fits.

fastsafetensors 0.4 provides a fit planner for exactly this: whole-file loads
while headroom is ample, per-file chunk budgets declining as the device fills.
Its budget is caller-supplied by design (`parallel_loader.py`, 0.4.0):

> **The caller picks the number — it knows what else lives on the device and,
> under broadcast loading, must pass the same value on every rank (e.g.
> all-reduce(MIN) of each rank's free memory)** so the plan stays identical
> across ranks.

This PR computes that budget from free device memory, agrees it across ranks
with all-reduce MIN, and passes it — with `use_chunk_budget_as_allocation_size`
for how chunks are sized, `accumulate_resident` for whether the consumer's
memory grows during the load, and `BudgetInfeasibleError` handled for a plan
that cannot be satisfied. It raises the dependency floor from
`fastsafetensors >= 0.3.3` to `>= 0.4`, which is where the planner lands.

## meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B

Public checkpoint, 55.5 GiB in 2 shards: largest shard 46.52 GiB, largest tensor
2.505 GiB. Single 96 GB card, weight-load time from vLLM's own log line:

| loader | weight load |
| --- | ---: |
| default (`auto`) | 52.74 s |
| `fastsafetensors`, main + 0.4.0 | **OOM** — `Tried to allocate 46.52 GiB`, 38.31 GiB free |
| `fastsafetensors`, this PR | **10.16 s** |

The planner needs twice the largest tensor, 5.01 GiB. Reported independently by
the fastsafetensors maintainer on a single 80 GB A100/H100
(foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors#71).

## What this changes

- **Device memory budget**, derived from free device memory and reduced with
  all-reduce MIN so every rank plans identically. Shards larger than the budget
  load in sub-shard chunks, each capped at `2 x` the largest tensor the load
  keeps: a chunk must hold that tensor, the second copy lets the producer read
  ahead, and beyond it the cap stops binding (measured: `T` +7.4% load time,
  `2T` +2.4%, `4T` identical to uncapped). The budget carries the reason when
  it is absent -- asked for, residency not modellable, free memory unreadable,
  or no memory to reserve from -- so an unplanned load can be explained.
  Planned loads select buffered reads up front, since the 0.4 GDS copier cannot
  chunk; `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET=0` selects GDS instead.
- **`accumulate_resident=False`.** Every quant method reachable from this loader
  creates its parameters at model-init time, so the load only copies into memory
  already allocated — measured on the default path, free device memory is
  unchanged across `load_weights()`. Online quantization is the exception: it
  materializes a smaller quantized parameter than the bytes it reads, which the
  plan would over-charge, so those loads are left unplanned unless a budget is
  set explicitly.
- **The budget all-reduce is unconditional**, with `0` meaning unbounded. A rank
  returning early — no reading, too little free memory, an unplannable consumer —
  would leave the others blocked in the reduce while it went on to the loader's
  broadcast sequence.
- **An infeasible plan raises**, naming the shortfall, rather than falling back
  to whole-shard staging — which needs a buffer at least as large as the tensor
  the plan could not place, so it is more likely to run out of memory, not less.
- **`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_ALL_LOCAL`** (opt-in, off by default). Every rank reads
  the whole checkpoint from storage instead of one rank reading and
  broadcasting. Enable it when ranks read from storage they do not share: on
  2x GB10 over RoCE, each node reading its own NVMe copy loads
  Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 in 16.6 s against 21.8 s broadcasting (n=2 per arm,
  non-overlapping). On a single node whose ranks share one NVMe it is a loss
  (43.2 s against 29.6 s), because the extra reads land on the contended device
  and the broadcast being avoided is cheap.
- **`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET`** overrides the derived budget;
  `0` removes the bound and stages whole shards. An escape hatch for a plan you
  believe is wrong, not a remedy for insufficient memory — and not the only
  route to an unbounded load, since one also runs unbounded when no budget can
  be derived.

Docs: `LoadConfig.load_format` now lists `"fastsafetensors"`, and the extension
page gains `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE`, the TP>1 GDS behavior, when
`ALL_LOCAL` pays, the online-quant exemption, and the `2 x largest tensor`
planning floor that decides whether a checkpoint is loadable by this format.

## Found deploying it at TP4 + DCP2 on 4x GB10 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 475 GiB)

- **Budget agreed on gloo, not CUDA over `WORLD`.** vLLM computes on the
  TP/DCP/EP subgroups, so `WORLD` often has no NCCL communicator at load time
  and the 8-byte budget `all_reduce` created one. NCCL's proxy connect pins
  ~9.19 MiB of host memory per connection for the communicator's lifetime,
  invisible to `torch.cuda.host_memory_stats()`. Reducing on
  `get_world_group().cpu_group` issues no NCCL collective during the load, as
  `--load-format auto` issues none. Host `Shmem` after load:

  | | Shmem after load | MemAvailable after release | boot |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
  | `--load-format auto` | 8.21 GiB (+0.00) | 31.08 GiB | healthy |
  | fastsafetensors, CUDA reduce | 12.06 GiB (**+3.85**) | 27.60 GiB | dies in FlashInfer autotune |
  | fastsafetensors, gloo reduce | 8.35 GiB (**+0.13**) | 30.12 GiB | healthy |

  Wasteful on a discrete GPU; on unified memory it comes out of the pool that
  KV cache and graph capture need.
- **EP filter honoured.** `default_loader` did not pass `local_expert_ids` to
  `fastsafetensors_weights_iterator`, so under expert parallelism this format
  read every expert while `auto` skips the ones the rank does not own (experts
  are ~85-90% of weight bytes). Now both formats select the same tensors. A
  `tensor_filter` is incompatible with broadcast, so a filtered load reads
  all-local. Verified on Qwen3-Coder-Next-FP8 (512 experts) at TP2 +
  `--enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter`: `loading 256/512
  experts` on both ranks, and generations byte-identical to `auto`.
- **Chunk cap sized from kept tensors.** `_safetensors_largest_tensor` takes the
  loader's predicate, so a tensor that is never read cannot set the cap. With
  DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's on-disk Engram tables it was 183 GiB instead of
  2.47 GiB, and the cap bounded nothing.

With all three the model boots and serves (count-to-100 exact, 30/30
structured-output gate, 7/7 vision + tool calling, KV pool unchanged), loading
in 54-63 s per rank against 133-177 s for `auto` on the same local shards.

## Validation

Three tests added to `tests/model_executor/model_loader/fastsafetensors_loader/`:

- `test_fastsafetensors_sub_shard_chunking` — a 384 MiB budget forces GPT-2's
  522 MiB shard to load as four chunks, which must still match
  `safetensors_weights_iterator` bitwise.
- `test_fastsafetensors_budget_infeasible` — a 1 MiB budget must raise
  `BudgetInfeasibleError` naming the shortfall, covering the no-fallback policy.
- `test_fastsafetensors_accumulate_resident_skips_derived_budget` — the same
  budget that raises above must load when the consumer's residency cannot be
  modelled, covering the online-quant exemption.

All run single-rank. At TP=2 on a checkpoint that already fits
(DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 3.4 GiB shards) load time is unchanged: 29.26 / 29.62 /
29.68 s against 28.62 / 30.00 s for stock.

Rebased on `19b0efce3`. On GB10 at `47232f3c7` (torch 2.14.0) with fastsafetensors
0.4.0, the `fastsafetensors_loader/` suite goes from 3 passed (base) to 6 passed. Upstream
#60152 now filters the shard list before this iterator; the planner sees
the filtered list, identically on every rank.

Lockfiles (`requirements/test/{cpu,cuda,rocm}.txt`) regenerated against
fastsafetensors 0.4.0 — one line per file, no other dependency changes.

## Model evaluation

This changes how weight bytes reach the device, not what they are; the chunking
path asserts bitwise equality against the reference safetensors iterator.

Generation across loaders at TP=2 with expert parallelism on DeepSeek-V4-Flash
was correct and coherent in every configuration. Token-level identity is not
asserted — that configuration is not reproducible run-to-run even at
`temperature=0` with a fixed seed.

## Duplicate check

Nothing open addresses this. The adjacent PRs are complementary:

- **#51554** adds a `fastsafetensors_sharded` load format in
  `sharded_state_loader.py` for pre-sharded checkpoints; this PR changes the
  default `fastsafetensors` path in `weight_utils.py`. The two touch
  `docs/models/extensions/fastsafetensor.md` in common — happy to rebase around
  whichever lands first.
- **#54416** (merged) fixes a PP draft-model deadlock by falling back to the
  standard loader; different failure, different code path.
- **#57973** (safetensors prefetch, successor to #52462) and **#53901** (ROCm PP)
  are unrelated axes.

## Upstream coordination

The fastsafetensors changes this depends on are merged and released in 0.4.0
(foundation-model-stack #81, #90, #91, #108). `BudgetInfeasibleError` is
exported from the package root, so vLLM catches it without importing a private
module. Design discussion: foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors#71.

## AI assistance disclosure

Claude Code was used to survey the integration points, draft the loader change,
docs and tests, and run pre-commit; and to run and analyse the measurements
reported above. The submitter authored the original loader integration (#40183),
produced the benchmark results on their own hardware, has reviewed every changed
line, and will maintain the contribution and respond to review feedback.

Agreed the four states shouldn't collapse onto `0` — fixed in 6de72dda8. The budget now returns why alongside the value, so an unplanned load says which of *asked for*, *residency not modellable*, *free memory unreadable*, or *no memory to reserve from* it was.

On raising when the derived budget is exhausted: I went looking for the case that justifies it and couldn't find one. `free <= 1 GiB` doesn't imply the load can't succeed — a checkpoint with 200 MB shards loads unplanned in 900 MB, so raising there would break a working load.

While there I tried to justify falling back to whole-shard staging when a plan is infeasible, and it has no regime. `fit_queue_size` clamps the pipeline before `plan_file_budgets`, so the single-rank floor is `2 x largest_tensor`, not `3 x`; unplanned staging must hold a whole shard plus a clone, so it is `>= 2T` — a tie at best, never cheaper. Measured on a checkpoint of alternating single-tensor shards built specifically to favour unplanned: planned 6.50 GiB against unplanned 7.00 GiB.

So the states get distinguished, and your no-fallback position from #71 stands unchanged.

Agreed, and it's worse than stated: on a GDS-capable host today the loader is constructed twice and prints a false "GDS not enabled" warning on every load. `GdsFileCopier` overrides neither `set_chunk` nor `chunk_transient_multiplier`, so the base raises `NotImplementedError` — a `RuntimeError` whose message contains "gds", which our own fallback handler then swallows.

Fixed in 6de72dda8: planning selects buffered reads up front, so there's no failed construction and no misleading warning.

That makes planning and GDS mutually exclusive in 0.4.0, so vLLM has to choose. We choose planning — running out of memory fails a load, buffered reads only slow it — with `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET=0` as the documented way to select GDS instead. Both the trade and the escape hatch are now in the docs page.

I have no GDS-capable host, so this is read from 0.4.0's source and a unit test rather than observed.

Taking the cap; declining the power-of-two rounding. Both in 6de72dda8, now `2 x largest_tensor`.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash has `largest_tensor = 0.9863 GiB`, so `pow2(T) = 1.0 GiB` — 1.4% headroom, about the worst case the rounding produces. Warm cache, n >= 2:

| cap | load time | allocated |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `T` (pow2 here) | 35.9 s | 2.05 GiB |
| `2T` | 34.3 s | 3.47 GiB |
| uncapped | 33.5 s | 6.77 GiB |

`2T` costs +2.4%, the pow2 cliff +7.4%. `4T` is byte-identical to uncapped, because it exceeds the largest shard and the cap stops binding — so `2T` sits mid-slope rather than on a plateau.

It's a trade rather than a dismissal: pow2 does allocate less. In our regime, buying ~1.4 GiB we have no use for at 4.9% of load time is the wrong side of it; on a device where that GiB mattered your rounding would be the better choice. The cliff is why I'd rather not have the multiple depend on where `T` falls relative to a power of two — clean hidden dimensions and stacked MoE experts land on them routinely.

One thing worth noting since it isn't visible from the diff: the cap that was there before this change (largest *shard*) never bound where the planner was already chunking, so it was a no-op on exactly the checkpoints it was meant for.

> under broadcast loading, must pass the same value on every rank (e.g.
> all-reduce(MIN) of each rank's free memory)** so the plan stays identical
> across ranks.

This PR computes that budget from free device memory, agrees it across ranks
with all-reduce MIN, and passes it — with `use_chunk_budget_as_allocation_size`
for how chunks are sized, `accumulate_resident` for whether the consumer's
memory grows during the load, and `BudgetInfeasibleError` handled for a plan
that cannot be satisfied. It raises the dependency floor from
`fastsafetensors >= 0.3.3` to `>= 0.4`, which is where the planner lands.

## meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B

Public checkpoint, 55.5 GiB in 2 shards: largest shard 46.52 GiB, largest tensor
2.505 GiB. Single 96 GB card, weight-load time from vLLM's own log line:

| loader | weight load |
| --- | ---: |
| default (`auto`) | 52.74 s |
| `fastsafetensors`, main + 0.4.0 | **OOM** — `Tried to allocate 46.52 GiB`, 38.31 GiB free |
| `fastsafetensors`, this PR | **10.16 s** |

The planner needs twice the largest tensor, 5.01 GiB. Reported independently by
the fastsafetensors maintainer on a single 80 GB A100/H100
(foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors#71).

## What this changes

- **Device memory budget**, derived from free device memory and reduced with
  all-reduce MIN so every rank plans identically. Shards larger than the budget
  load in sub-shard chunks, each capped at `2 x` the largest tensor the load
  keeps: a chunk must hold that tensor, the second copy lets the producer read
  ahead, and beyond it the cap stops binding (measured: `T` +7.4% load time,
  `2T` +2.4%, `4T` identical to uncapped). The budget carries the reason when
  it is absent -- asked for, residency not modellable, free memory unreadable,
  or no memory to reserve from -- so an unplanned load can be explained.
  Planned loads select buffered reads up front, since the 0.4 GDS copier cannot
  chunk; `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET=0` selects GDS instead.
- **`accumulate_resident=False`.** Every quant method reachable from this loader
  creates its parameters at model-init time, so the load only copies into memory
  already allocated — measured on the default path, free device memory is
  unchanged across `load_weights()`. Online quantization is the exception: it
  materializes a smaller quantized parameter than the bytes it reads, which the
  plan would over-charge, so those loads are left unplanned unless a budget is
  set explicitly.
- **The budget all-reduce is unconditional**, with `0` meaning unbounded. A rank
  returning early — no reading, too little free memory, an unplannable consumer —
  would leave the others blocked in the reduce while it went on to the loader's
  broadcast sequence.
- **An infeasible plan raises**, naming the shortfall, rather than falling back
  to whole-shard staging — which needs a buffer at least as large as the tensor
  the plan could not place, so it is more likely to run out of memory, not less.
- **`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_ALL_LOCAL`** (opt-in, off by default). Every rank reads
  the whole checkpoint from storage instead of one rank reading and
  broadcasting. Enable it when ranks read from storage they do not share: on
  2x GB10 over RoCE, each node reading its own NVMe copy loads
  Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 in 16.6 s against 21.8 s broadcasting (n=2 per arm,
  non-overlapping). On a single node whose ranks share one NVMe it is a loss
  (43.2 s against 29.6 s), because the extra reads land on the contended device
  and the broadcast being avoided is cheap.
- **`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET`** overrides the derived budget;
  `0` removes the bound and stages whole shards. An escape hatch for a plan you
  believe is wrong, not a remedy for insufficient memory — and not the only
  route to an unbounded load, since one also runs unbounded when no budget can
  be derived.

Docs: `LoadConfig.load_format` now lists `"fastsafetensors"`, and the extension
page gains `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE`, the TP>1 GDS behavior, when
`ALL_LOCAL` pays, the online-quant exemption, and the `2 x largest tensor`
planning floor that decides whether a checkpoint is loadable by this format.

## Found deploying it at TP4 + DCP2 on 4x GB10 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 475 GiB)

- **Budget agreed on gloo, not CUDA over `WORLD`.** vLLM computes on the
  TP/DCP/EP subgroups, so `WORLD` often has no NCCL communicator at load time
  and the 8-byte budget `all_reduce` created one. NCCL's proxy connect pins
  ~9.19 MiB of host memory per connection for the communicator's lifetime,
  invisible to `torch.cuda.host_memory_stats()`. Reducing on
  `get_world_group().cpu_group` issues no NCCL collective during the load, as
  `--load-format auto` issues none. Host `Shmem` after load:

  | | Shmem after load | MemAvailable after release | boot |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
  | `--load-format auto` | 8.21 GiB (+0.00) | 31.08 GiB | healthy |
  | fastsafetensors, CUDA reduce | 12.06 GiB (**+3.85**) | 27.60 GiB | dies in FlashInfer autotune |
  | fastsafetensors, gloo reduce | 8.35 GiB (**+0.13**) | 30.12 GiB | healthy |

  Wasteful on a discrete GPU; on unified memory it comes out of the pool that
  KV cache and graph capture need.
- **EP filter honoured.** `default_loader` did not pass `local_expert_ids` to
  `fastsafetensors_weights_iterator`, so under expert parallelism this format
  read every expert while `auto` skips the ones the rank does not own (experts
  are ~85-90% of weight bytes). Now both formats select the same tensors. A
  `tensor_filter` is incompatible with broadcast, so a filtered load reads
  all-local. Verified on Qwen3-Coder-Next-FP8 (512 experts) at TP2 +
  `--enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter`: `loading 256/512
  experts` on both ranks, and generations byte-identical to `auto`.
- **Chunk cap sized from kept tensors.** `_safetensors_largest_tensor` takes the
  loader's predicate, so a tensor that is never read cannot set the cap. With
  DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's on-disk Engram tables it was 183 GiB instead of
  2.47 GiB, and the cap bounded nothing.

With all three the model boots and serves (count-to-100 exact, 30/30
structured-output gate, 7/7 vision + tool calling, KV pool unchanged), loading
in 54-63 s per rank against 133-177 s for `auto` on the same local shards.

## Validation

Three tests added to `tests/model_executor/model_loader/fastsafetensors_loader/`:

- `test_fastsafetensors_sub_shard_chunking` — a 384 MiB budget forces GPT-2's
  522 MiB shard to load as four chunks, which must still match
  `safetensors_weights_iterator` bitwise.
- `test_fastsafetensors_budget_infeasible` — a 1 MiB budget must raise
  `BudgetInfeasibleError` naming the shortfall, covering the no-fallback policy.
- `test_fastsafetensors_accumulate_resident_skips_derived_budget` — the same
  budget that raises above must load when the consumer's residency cannot be
  modelled, covering the online-quant exemption.

All run single-rank. At TP=2 on a checkpoint that already fits
(DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 3.4 GiB shards) load time is unchanged: 29.26 / 29.62 /
29.68 s against 28.62 / 30.00 s for stock.

Rebased on `19b0efce3`. On GB10 at `47232f3c7` (torch 2.14.0) with fastsafetensors
0.4.0, the `fastsafetensors_loader/` suite goes from 3 passed (base) to 6 passed. Upstream
#60152 now filters the shard list before this iterator; the planner sees
the filtered list, identically on every rank.

Lockfiles (`requirements/test/{cpu,cuda,rocm}.txt`) regenerated against
fastsafetensors 0.4.0 — one line per file, no other dependency changes.

## Model evaluation

This changes how weight bytes reach the device, not what they are; the chunking
path asserts bitwise equality against the reference safetensors iterator.

Generation across loaders at TP=2 with expert parallelism on DeepSeek-V4-Flash
was correct and coherent in every configuration. Token-level identity is not
asserted — that configuration is not reproducible run-to-run even at
`temperature=0` with a fixed seed.

## Duplicate check

Nothing open addresses this. The adjacent PRs are complementary:

- **#51554** adds a `fastsafetensors_sharded` load format in
  `sharded_state_loader.py` for pre-sharded checkpoints; this PR changes the
  default `fastsafetensors` path in `weight_utils.py`. The two touch
  `docs/models/extensions/fastsafetensor.md` in common — happy to rebase around
  whichever lands first.
- **#54416** (merged) fixes a PP draft-model deadlock by falling back to the
  standard loader; different failure, different code path.
- **#57973** (safetensors prefetch, successor to #52462) and **#53901** (ROCm PP)
  are unrelated axes.

## Upstream coordination

The fastsafetensors changes this depends on are merged and released in 0.4.0
(foundation-model-stack #81, #90, #91, #108). `BudgetInfeasibleError` is
exported from the package root, so vLLM catches it without importing a private
module. Design discussion: foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors#71.

## AI assistance disclosure

Claude Code was used to survey the integration points, draft the loader change,
docs and tests, and run pre-commit; and to run and analyse the measurements
reported above. The submitter authored the original loader integration (#40183),
produced the benchmark results on their own hardware, has reviewed every changed
line, and will maintain the contribution and respond to review feedback.

@@ -4,3 +4,57 @@ Loading model weights with fastsafetensors
 Using fastsafetensors library enables loading model weights to GPU memory by leveraging GPU direct storage. See [their GitHub repository](https://github.com/foundation-model-stack/fastsafetensors) for more details.
 
 To enable this feature, use the `--load-format fastsafetensors` command-line argument
+
+The loader requires a CUDA or ROCm device. GPUDirect Storage is used when tensor
+parallelism is disabled; with `--tensor-parallel-size` greater than 1 it is turned
+off, because initializing the GDS DMA subsystem creates a CUDA context on every
+visible GPU. vLLM also falls back to buffered reads when the checkpoint sits on a
+filesystem without GDS support.
+
+Tuning
+------
+
+`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE` (default `0`) pipelines shard loading: the
+producer prepares the next shard while the consumer copies the current one into
+model parameters. Each increment holds one additional shard-sized device buffer
+at peak, so the default keeps the non-pipelined memory footprint.
+
+`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_ALL_LOCAL` (default `0`) has every rank read its weights
+from storage instead of one rank reading and broadcasting. Every rank reads the
+full checkpoint rather than 1/N of it, so whether that pays depends on which
+resource the ranks compete for: enable it when each rank reads storage it does
+not share, where the extra reads land on idle devices and replace a slower
+broadcast across nodes. Leave it disabled when ranks share one device, whether
+local or network, because the extra reads then contend for the resource the load
+is already waiting on and the broadcast they avoid is comparatively cheap.
+
+Measured both ways: four GB10 ranks reading a per-node copy over RoCE loaded a
+118 GiB checkpoint in 16.6 s against 21.8 s broadcasting, while two GPUs sharing
+one NVMe took 43.2 s against 29.6 s.
+
+vLLM plans each shard against the device memory left free after the model
+parameters are allocated, so a checkpoint that nearly fills the GPU is loaded in
+sub-shard chunks rather than staged whole. Online quantization is exempt: it
+keeps parameters on the meta device and materializes a smaller quantized
+parameter than the bytes it reads, which the plan cannot model, so those loads
+are left unplanned unless a budget is set explicitly.
+
+`VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET` overrides that derived budget in
+bytes. When no feasible plan exists the load stops with an error naming the
+shortfall. It does not fall back to staging whole shards, because that needs a
+buffer at least as large as the tensor the plan could not place, and so is more
+likely to run out of memory rather than less.
+
+The plan's floor is twice the largest single tensor: a shard can always be
+split, a tensor cannot, and the copy is double-buffered. A checkpoint whose
+largest tensor does not fit twice over in free device memory therefore cannot be
+loaded by this format at all. The default loader (`--load-format auto`) copies
+tensor by tensor from lazy mmap and needs no shard-sized staging buffer, so it
+remains able to load such a checkpoint, more slowly.
+
+Setting the budget to `0` removes the memory bound and stages whole shards. That
+is an escape hatch for a plan you believe is wrong, not a fix for insufficient
+memory: on a checkpoint that needed a bound, it is likely to run out of memory
+during loading. Loads also run unbounded when no budget can be derived -- free
+memory could not be read, or too little is free to reserve headroom from -- so
+an unplanned load is not always a deliberate choice.

Agreed the four states shouldn't collapse onto `0` — fixed in 6de72dda8. The budget now returns why alongside the value, so an unplanned load says which of *asked for*, *residency not modellable*, *free memory unreadable*, or *no memory to reserve from* it was.

Agreed, and it's worse than stated: on a GDS-capable host today the loader is constructed twice and prints a false "GDS not enabled" warning on every load. `GdsFileCopier` overrides neither `set_chunk` nor `chunk_transient_multiplier`, so the base raises `NotImplementedError` — a `RuntimeError` whose message contains "gds", which our own fallback handler then swallows.

Fixed in 6de72dda8: planning selects buffered reads up front, so there's no failed construction and no misleading warning.

That makes planning and GDS mutually exclusive in 0.4.0, so vLLM has to choose. We choose planning — running out of memory fails a load, buffered reads only slow it — with `VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET=0` as the documented way to select GDS instead. Both the trade and the escape hatch are now in the docs page.

I have no GDS-capable host, so this is read from 0.4.0's source and a unit test rather than observed.

Taking the cap; declining the power-of-two rounding. Both in 6de72dda8, now `2 x largest_tensor`.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash has `largest_tensor = 0.9863 GiB`, so `pow2(T) = 1.0 GiB` — 1.4% headroom, about the worst case the rounding produces. Warm cache, n >= 2:

| cap | load time | allocated |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `T` (pow2 here) | 35.9 s | 2.05 GiB |
| `2T` | 34.3 s | 3.47 GiB |
| uncapped | 33.5 s | 6.77 GiB |

`2T` costs +2.4%, the pow2 cliff +7.4%. `4T` is byte-identical to uncapped, because it exceeds the largest shard and the cap stops binding — so `2T` sits mid-slope rather than on a plateau.

It's a trade rather than a dismissal: pow2 does allocate less. In our regime, buying ~1.4 GiB we have no use for at 4.9% of load time is the wrong side of it; on a device where that GiB mattered your rounding would be the better choice. The cliff is why I'd rather not have the multiple depend on where `T` falls relative to a power of two — clean hidden dimensions and stacked MoE experts land on them routinely.

One thing worth noting since it isn't visible from the diff: the cap that was there before this change (largest *shard*) never bound where the planner was already chunking, so it was a no-op on exactly the checkpoints it was meant for.

Thanks @takeshi-yoshimura — all three addressed in 6de72dda8, pushed as a separate commit so the delta is readable. Replies inline; two things that aren't line-specific:

**`use_chunk_budget_as_allocation_size` is dropped.** It allocated every chunk at the planner's budget rather than its span, so staging tracked available memory instead of the checkpoint: at a derived budget on DeepSeek-V4-Flash it reserved 24.0 GiB to move 6.8 GiB of tensors. It does suppress fragmentation — the reserved/allocated gap goes from 15.3 GiB to 0.9 GiB — but it pays for that in memory that binds, to save memory the caching allocator hands back on demand. Measured: a 155 GiB checkpoint completes with 1.18 GiB of headroom over its live requirement and 5 allocator retries, so allocated is the quantity that constrains and reserved is not.

**Four suggestions for a future release**, all originating in your review here rather than from taste, which I'll file separately on the fastsafetensors tracker: a public header-stats helper so callers don't reparse the format; defaulting `max_batch_bytes` from the largest kept tensor when a budget is set (your suggestion, as a library default); structured fields on `BudgetInfeasibleError`; and `set_chunk`/`chunk_transient_multiplier` on `GdsFileCopier`, which is the only thing that makes the GDS trade above go away rather than be documented around.

Also — could a maintainer add the `ready` label? CI hasn't run on this PR at all: `pre-run-check` gates it behind a label or 4+ merged PRs, and I have one. I've run the fastsafetensors suite (6 passed) and `pre-commit` (13 hooks, clean) locally on an RTX PRO 6000, but that's no substitute for CI seeing it.

Context on `Amendment C`, since three lines understate it.

The budget `all_reduce` reduces over `WORLD` with a CUDA tensor. vLLM computes on the TP/DCP/EP subgroups, so `WORLD` often has no NCCL communicator yet and this call creates one — and NCCL's proxy connect then pins ~9.19 MiB of host memory per proxy connection for the communicator's lifetime, invisible to `torch.cuda.host_memory_stats()`. Measured on 4× DGX Spark (GB10), TP4 + DCP2, host `Shmem` after load:

| | Shmem after load | boot |
|---|---|---|
| `--load-format auto` | 8.21 GiB (+0.00) | healthy |
| this PR, before C | 12.06 GiB (**+3.85**) | dies in FlashInfer autotune |
| this PR, with C | 8.35 GiB (**+0.13**) | healthy |

`auto` issues no collective while loading, so it pays none of this. Wasteful on a discrete GPU; on unified memory it comes out of the same pool as KV and graph capture, which is what blocked the boot.

Happy to add a `fastsafetensor.md` note and a test that the agreement runs on a gloo group (the failure mode is silent), or to split C into its own PR if you'd rather keep this one to the fit planner.
